definition.description: Fetches all users from Microsoft Graph API with automatic pagination. Retrieves user profiles including display name, email, job title, and other directory attributes. Supports field selection to optimize payload size and configurable page limits for large directories. Uses OData pagination (@odata.nextLink) to iterate through all results.

inputFields.helpText: Microsoft Graph OAuth access token with User.Read.All or Directory.Read.All permissions. Obtain via OAuth 2.0 flow or use the Connector Token node.
Maximum number of pages to fetch. Acts as a safety limit to prevent runaway requests in large directories. Set to a higher value for complete enumeration.
Number of users to retrieve per API request. Microsoft Graph supports up to 999 per page. Larger values reduce API calls but increase response time per request.

Comma-separated list of user properties to return (e.g., id,displayName,mail,userPrincipalName,jobTitle). Reduces response payload and improves performance. Leave empty to return all default properties.

outputParameters.description: Array containing all retrieved user objects with their properties (id, displayName, mail, userPrincipalName, etc.)
Serialized JSON string of all users array, ready for storage or transmission to external systems
Total count of user objects retrieved across all pages. May be less than directory total if maxPages limit was reached.
Number of API requests made during pagination. Useful for monitoring API consumption and optimizing page size.
Boolean flag indicating if any errors occurred during the fetch operation. Check ErrorMessage for details when true.
Detailed error message including HTTP status code, page number where failure occurred, and exception details if applicable

connectionTags.description: Triggered when all pages were fetched successfully and at least one user was found
Triggered when an API error, HTTP failure, or exception occurs during any page fetch
Triggered when the API returns successfully but the directory contains no users matching the query
